stories.title: Venezuela quakes kill nearly 1,000, over 50,000 missing
stories.summary: Desperate Venezuelans and rescue teams are racing to find survivors after the death toll from twin earthquakes rose above 900, with foreign crews and aid only beginning to reach devastated areas nearly two days after the quakes. The government said 172 people remained trapped, 920 were dead and 3,360 injured after the quakes devastated parts of Caracas and surrounding areas on Wednesday evening. Caracas residents jeered interim leader Delcy Rodriguez during her visit to a devastated neighborhood, as fury over the perceived lack of an official response mounted. United Nations aid chief Tom Fletcher said that more than 50,000 people were missing after two powerful earthquakes struck within a minute of each other on Wednesday evening, flattening buildings in the north of the country.

stories.title: US, Iran trade strikes putting new strain on truce
stories.summary: Iran has launched attacks on US sites in the Gulf in response to American strikes on the country, state media has said, after Washington accused Tehran of attacking one of its cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The trading of fire raised questions about efforts to keep the crucial waterway open while Washington and Tehran negotiate a final settlement to a war that began on 28 February with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. US Central Command said aircraft struck missile and drone storage locations and coastal radar sites, and a US official reported the operation had concluded. Iranian state television, citing a reporter in the southern port city of Sirik, said an explosion was heard late last night at Taherouyeh pier.

stories.title: Dunderrow women speak publicly after years of silence
stories.summary: This week, survivors of abuse at Dunderrow National School in Co Cork spoke publicly for the first time about the abuse they endured as children - and called for redress for the harm done to them. Their ordinariness belies the trauma they have carried since they were seven and eight years old. Mothers, sisters, aunts, grandmothers; they are women who we pass on the street without a second glance. Their childhoods were taken in a two-room State-run school in Dunderrow, Co Cork, during the 1960s and early 1970s, where they were sexually abused by their teacher, Leo Hickey.

stories.title: Record heatwave to spread east as Germany, Poland swelter
stories.summary: Germans are bracing for sweltering conditions as a heatwave linked to dozens of deaths in western Europe is forecast to move east and bring temperatures approaching 40C to Germany and Poland. Britain, France and Switzerland have baked in record heat in June, and the system was expected to test more records as the heatwave crosses the Rhine River. Public broadcaster ARD said a German record of over 41.3C was reached yesterday near Saarbruecken on the border with France, according to preliminary official data. In France, dozens of people, including both young and old, have died during the heatwave. Temperatures above 40C have disrupted rail travel and power generation, sparked alcohol bans, suspended schools and postponed outdoor events.

stories.title: Ireland's EU Presidency: What it is and why it matters
stories.summary: On Wednesday, the eyes of Europe will fall on Ireland as the State assumes the Presidency of the European Union. It will be the eighth time Ireland has taken on the role since we joined the EEC in 1973. However, compared to previous presidencies, given the cycle of crises the EU has confronted in recent years, the stakes could not be higher: The sheer volume of legislation that the Government will be expected to steer through the EU’s law-making machinery could not be greater. Back in 2013, the EU Presidency fell on a country still badly bruised by the banking crisis and subsequent EU/IMF bailout.

stories.title: Delight for Pico and Cape Verde as journey goes on
stories.summary: Cape Verde, with Shamrock Rovers' Pico Lopes in their ranks, have reached the knockout stage of the World Cup, becoming the smallest country in history to qualify for the next phase of the competition after a 0-0 draw against Saudi Arabia. Both teams struggled to create opportunities in front of the goal in the first half. An early attempt from Jamiro Monteiro was saved by Saudi goalkeeper Mohammed Al-Owais. In the second half, Al-Owais comfortably saved an effort from Wagner Pina, while Kevin Pina later shot wide.
